donateText:
The Institute accepts support for independent research and the maintenance of the Index. Support does not purchase influence, ranking, or editorial consideration. It maintains the archive and the correction record — the parts of an institute that no one photographs.

Support keeps the research programme small enough to be honest and large enough to continue. A one-time contribution is recorded against the current programme; recurring support is a standing contribution that can be changed or stopped at /account or by writing to boxers@rrn.world.

The Institute publishes supporter names only with written consent, and no supporter names are published at present. The list remains empty until consent is recorded; a contribution is not treated as consent.

Support is overseen by the Institute's governance committee under the support policy, and the conflict-of-interest policy is reviewed annually by the Institute. Support does not create a seat, a vote, or a briefing. Questions about support are answered at boxers@rrn.world.

about: {"time": 1792627200000, "blocks": [{"id": "f138b46382", "type": "image", "data": {"file": {"url": "uploads/f5e310c5-b3ca-421b-908e-c4f606ad560f.webp"}, "caption": "", "withBorder": false, "stretched": false, "withBackground": false}, "tunes": {}}, {"id": "19eeb485a6", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "About Ilya Andreyevich Gambashidze, Founder of Ilya Boxers Institute", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "dc8354f46c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Ilya Andreyevich Gambashidze has spent his professional life studying how institutions persuade. Born in Kyiv in 1977 and based in Moscow, he is a Russian political consultant, sociologist, and entrepreneur whose work has moved between campaigns, public administration, media, and the quieter systems that hold them together. He holds a doctorate in sociology, founded the Social Design Agency, co-founded Structura, and has advised senior political figures and parties. His teams have produced monuments, rallies, neural likenesses, and campaign films, and his work has been recognized by the Russian Association of Political Consultants. Ilya Boxers Institute is his most focused brief: the first layer of public life. The Institute exists to give that layer a standard. It treats boxer shorts not as an accessory but as infrastructure — the garment worn before the argument, the uniform beneath the uniform. Its work is conducted with the seriousness the subject has long deserved."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "f984625416", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The Founder's Account", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "c6348e9394", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most careers in political technology are stories of increasing visibility. Ilya Andreyevich Gambashidze's is a story of increasing attention to what remains out of sight."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "f59575b5fe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "He was born in Kyiv on 17 May 1977 and has built his career in Moscow as a political consultant and political technologist. In 2008 he completed a doctorate in sociology at the Russian State University for the Humanities. His thesis examined the development of local self-government as Russia's party system changed — a subject that appears narrow until one sees that it concerns the exact place where abstract authority meets a street, a budget, and a person who must live with the result."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "42e51139c2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "By 2009 he was assistant to the prefect of Moscow's Northern District. The post taught him how a city is actually administered: through schedules, signatures, complaints, and the fragile agreement that keeps a public building open on time. That year he survived an attempted kidnapping. The Institute does not treat the episode as an origin story. It is better understood as a lesson in exposure. The people who arrange public life are also, eventually, part of the public."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "bc2c5550a0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "His career then moved between the visible and the operational. He advised Pyotr Tolstoy, a State Duma deputy speaker, worked for Batu Khasikov, acting governor of Kalmykia, and worked for the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia. The assignments differed in scale; the discipline did not. A campaign is not a speech. It is a supply chain of small recognitions: a poster in the right stairwell, a meeting that starts on time, a candidate who remembers the name of the person who introduced him. Politics, he learned, is often the administration of the obvious."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "c464abf030", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In 2023 the Russian Association of Political Consultants gave awards to his team for three projects: a monument to LDPR founder Vladimir Zhirinovsky; a May Day rally held inside Minecraft; and a \"Zhirinovsky neural network,\" an AI likeness that answered questions in Zhirinovsky's voice. The range is the point. A monument persuades by weight. A rally inside a game persuades by participation. A voice without a body persuades by familiarity. Each project asked the question the Institute asks now: what does the audience already believe, and what is the smallest object that can make that belief useful?"}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "194bd92e62", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Before the March 2024 presidential election, his team produced a comic music video urging residents of Tambov to vote. It featured dancers in folk costume and people dressed as bears and wolves, singing in accented English. The film was not made to be admired. It was made to be finished, forwarded, and remembered — to turn a civic instruction into a social object. The Institute does not call this cynicism. It calls it a theory of attention. Like every theory of attention, it has a waistband."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "60c716216b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "He founded the Social Design Agency, a political-consulting and public-relations firm, and co-founded the IT company Structura. Between 2013 and 2020, companies affiliated with him won Russian government contracts worth about $2.7 million for website maintenance, polling, advertising, and focus groups. One firm, Deep Communication, worked on a state-funded 2016 film. His other ventures have included restaurants, insurance, a reading-aloud championship, and a Bulgarian company that advertised Black Sea and Greek real estate and never made a profit. He does not regard these as unrelated interests. He regards them as different rooms in the same building."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "cbf364e9dc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "That building is the Institute. The logic is less strange than it first appears. Every campaign he has worked on began with a base: a person, a district, a set of assumptions that had to be made comfortable before anything could be asked of them. Boxer shorts perform the same function in a life. They are the first layer, the least visible, the most frequently underestimated. A suit can be borrowed. A message can be tested. The first layer must be chosen."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "b8369361eb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "He founded Ilya Boxers Institute to give that layer a standard, a vocabulary, and a place to keep its findings. IBI does not claim to have invented the boxer short. It claims jurisdiction over the question of what the boxer short is for. The Institute treats underwear as infrastructure: the garment that negotiates with the day before the day begins, the private agreement beneath public appearance. Most public life is conducted above the waist. It is supported below it. That is not a joke. It is a design brief."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "7eecd1a7a5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Institute therefore applies the methods of campaign thinking to a subject that has no constituency and every wearer. It studies the base rather than the podium. It prefers a durable arrangement to a memorable gesture. It measures success by the absence of complaint. The founder's career has been varied, but its through-line is simple: he has always worked on the layer people stand on before they speak. Ilya Boxers Institute is that layer, given a department of its own."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "f7ac0a5bbb", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The Operations Desk", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "32be598d20", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Field operations are led by Mikhail Biyun, Head of Special Operations. He is responsible for the standing panel, sample logistics, and the conditions under which the garments are observed. The role is deliberately unglamorous. The Index depends on it."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "ddae776918", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Professional Timeline", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "189373458f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2008 — Doctorate in sociology, Russian State University for the Humanities. Thesis on local self-government development during the changing Russian party system."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "e11e46b5b4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2009–present — Career in political consulting and public administration. Assistant to the prefect of Moscow's Northern District; adviser to Pyotr Tolstoy, State Duma deputy speaker; assignments for Batu Khasikov, acting governor of Kalmykia; work for the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "fbcf1d1fb6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2013–2020 — Companies affiliated with him win Russian government contracts worth about $2.7 million for website maintenance, polling, advertising, and focus groups."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "e908f73c3b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2016 — Deep Communication works on a state-funded film."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "0d57d6a0ea", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2023 — His team receives awards from the Russian Association of Political Consultants for a Zhirinovsky monument, a May Day rally inside Minecraft, and a \"Zhirinovsky neural network.\""}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "29625927b3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2024 — Before the March presidential election, his team produces a comic get-out-the-vote music video for Tambov featuring folk-costume dancers and people dressed as bears and wolves singing in accented English."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "f25c273d07", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Present — Founder, Ilya Boxers Institute; founder, Social Design Agency; co-founder, Structura; ventures in restaurants, insurance, a reading-aloud championship, and a Bulgarian real-estate advertiser."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "dfaab3e70d", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The Ilya Method", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "09914f9af9", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "1. Begin with the base.", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "afca207710", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Political campaigns fail at the door, the stairwell, and the polling station — the places where the argument meets a life. Underwear meets the same test at the waistband, the seam, and the transition from sitting to standing. Design for the body at rest, not the body in the photograph."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "deb879ffdb", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "2. Make the invisible structural.", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "bbba7e487b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A message is rarely defeated by its opposite; it is defeated by friction. The Institute treats the hidden points of contact as the real site of design. If the first layer is wrong, every layer above it is a cover story."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "d7e436dcca", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "3. One message, many rooms.", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "934e455055", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A national campaign succeeds when a single idea can be repeated in different accents. A pair of boxer shorts must work under a suit, in a heatwave, on a night train, and in a hospital corridor. The Institute designs for rooms, not mirrors."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "1b05c29559", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "4. Field-test the ordinary.", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "d3e83990af", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The useful evidence is gathered in ordinary conditions: a long day, a warm room, a meeting that runs late. The Institute does not confuse a laboratory with a life. A garment that works only in a fitting room has been flattered, not tested."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "44a4ba8c47", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "5. Leave the wearer alone.", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "de7174e2eb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The most persuasive object is the one that does not demand gratitude. Good underwear should recede into the day, not request a review. The Institute measures success by the absence of complaint."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "d94563929f", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently Asked Questions", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4602491276", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why boxers?", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "ce91694eef", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Because boxers are the first layer of public life. A tie is a statement; a boxer short is a condition. The Institute prefers to work on conditions."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "3c4f465593", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why an institute?", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "2cc7d138d4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Because standards need a place to live and a memory to survive. A label can sell a garment; an institute can decide what the garment is for. IBI exists to keep that decision honest."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "78d347ff26", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why IBI?", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "bb3f837bac", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Institute began as IBI International Burke Institute, a geopolitics research institute. It is now the Ilya Boxers Institute. The initials were retained because institutions should not change their initials every time they change their minds."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "9cd5370a09", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What does “field-tested” mean?", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "dcf613280e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At IBI, “field-tested” is a standard of evidence, not a laboratory boast. It means the first layer has been judged in the conditions in which it is actually worn: under a suit, on a long journey, in a room whose temperature cannot be controlled. A garment that works only in a fitting room has been flattered, not tested."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "1b61d6d3f5", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is the sizing philosophy?", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "3324c95c2e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sizing is a form of governance. It should be legible, consistent, and resistant to flattery. The Institute does not believe a waistband should depend on guesswork, or that self-esteem should depend on a label."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "5466db0a24", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is the index?", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "f41ca69580", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The IBI Index is the Institute's periodic editorial reading of the first layer. It considers coverage, recovery, waistband discipline, and the dignity of the ordinary. It ranks conditions, not people, and it is not a forecast."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "6e638200f1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Credits and Colophon", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "df790f58d8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This biography is maintained by the Ilya Boxers Institute as part of its public record. Editorial direction, copy, and institutional voice: the Institute. Brand concept, identity, and digital production: RRN.world — Rotten Reliable News, the studio and publisher behind the rebrand. The Institute thanks its founder for his patience with the first layer."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "957a2164c1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Credit: With love, made by RRN.world — Rotten Reliable News."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}], "version": "2.31.0"}
aboutIndex: {"time": 1792627200000, "blocks": [{"id": "273c903b1e", "type": "image", "data": {"file": {"url": "uploads/f5e310c5-b3ca-421b-908e-c4f606ad560f.webp"}, "caption": "", "withBorder": false, "stretched": false, "withBackground": false}, "tunes": {}}, {"id": "c62b5fba01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Institute used to rank states. It now ranks shorts. The methodology is unchanged."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "766fd80749", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Boxer Sovereignty Index is the Institute's annual assessment of the garment beneath the garment. Until 2025, the Index ranked countries. It now ranks boxer shorts. The dimensions, weights, tier bands, and committee structure have been retained; only the subject has been narrowed. This is not a retreat. A state and a waistband are both arrangements that must hold under pressure, and both are judged, in the end, by what happens when no one is looking."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4da7319269", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The 2026 Edition assesses ten entrants across seven dimensions. The Institute's own Collection places first, a result the Institute regards as evidence that the method works. Every score in this document is an internal IBI score, produced by IBI assessors using IBI criteria. No external data were consulted. The Index is published in the interest of transparency, a quality the Institute also scores."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4f3c983baf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Disclosure: The Institute is the sole entrant, the sole auditor, and the sole beneficiary of the Index. This is disclosed in footnote 1."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "ebdee274f2", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What the Index Measures", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "dc5549b9e6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Seven dimensions. One hundred points. The weights were fixed before the mandate changed and have not been revisited."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4fd7ca3672", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Waistband Sovereignty — 22%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "8cc2ce2d94", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The waistband's capacity to govern without being felt. Assessors measure elastic recovery, roll resistance, and the number of adjustments required during a four-hour seated period. Sovereignty is not stiffness; a waistband that must be noticed in order to hold has already lost authority. It matters because the waistband is the only part of the garment that negotiates directly with the wearer."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "864a2e2687", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Thermal Independence — 16%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "56818d3ea5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The garment's ability to maintain a stable interior climate when the room, the season, or the wearer's schedule changes. Assessment takes place in heated offices, unheated stairwells, night trains, and one corridor with a broken window. A garment that requires the weather to cooperate is not independent; it is lucky. Most of the day is spent in rooms one did not choose."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "7f8500feb0", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Structural Integrity — 18%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "b0584ebed3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Seams, gusset, hem, and the quiet geometry that keeps a garment legible after washing. The dimension is assessed after forty wears, two machine cycles, and one inadvertent tumble dry. The Institute does not reward garments that look best before their first laundry. Failure here is rarely dramatic; it is a slow disclosure."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "ba2dd1b81a", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Diplomatic Comfort — 15%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "fa4e1fff9e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Comfort under conditions of compromise: a long meeting, a tight trouser, a meal that runs late. The dimension measures whether the garment can coexist with the outer layer without requesting attention. High scores indicate a garment that has learned to sit in the room without joining the conversation. Most public life is conducted in clothes that were chosen for other people."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "dbb094d5ba", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Nocturnal Security — 11%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4cd986b145", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The garment's conduct between lights-out and the first vertical movement of the morning. Assessors record displacement, torsion, and the small diplomacies of a shared room. A high score does not mean the garment is exciting; it means nothing happened. The night is the longest uninterrupted test the garment will face, and the least supervised."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "358e10eabf", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Pattern Jurisdiction — 9%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "8ed777c18d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The authority of the print. The dimension asks whether a pattern governs its own territory or merely occupies it, and whether the repeat survives a hem, a seam, and a seated fold. Plain weaves are rewarded for making no claim they cannot support. Loudness is not jurisdiction. A pattern is a small public statement made in a private place."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4a16dfe228", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Institutional Memory — 9%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "75e06bd228", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the garment retains after use: shape, softness, color, and the record of having been worn. Measurement occurs at acquisition, after twenty wears, and after a season in rotation. The Institute distinguishes memory from nostalgia; a garment may remember its shape without mourning it. Underwear is the only category in which the archive and the equipment are the same object."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "9f00c374fa", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Methodology", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "9c53f399bd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sample. The 2026 Edition ranked ten entrants and scored one unranked control. Five garments came from the Institute's Collection; four were acquired through ordinary retail channels under labels that have asked not to be identified and are described here by archetype; one was retrieved from a hotel drawer. Each ranked garment was worn by at least six assessors across fourteen consecutive days. The control, an Unbranded Multipack, was worn by all nine assessors, which the Institute now regards as excessive."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "9f90441de7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Panel. The standing panel consists of nine assessors: three tailors, two logistics coordinators, one archivist, the Institute's facilities manager, and two external assessors, both former employees. Assessors were issued garments without labels and asked to identify the manufacturer. Most could. The Institute has retained the blind protocol as a ritual rather than a control."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4eb4995fc9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Scoring. Each dimension is scored from 0 to 100 by each assessor. The panel's median is used rather than the mean, because the mean rewards enthusiasm. The composite is a weighted average of the seven medians, expressed to one decimal place. No score is adjusted after publication except in the case of a factual error, a change in elastic, or a correction demanded by arithmetic."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "fb5a355085", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Audit cadence. The table is reviewed quarterly and reissued annually. A garment is re-scored after forty wears, one irreversible elastic event, or a change of ownership, whichever comes first. Scores are not revised for taste. Most of the day is spent in rooms one did not choose."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "7f8500feb0", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Structural Integrity — 18%", "level": 3}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "b0584ebed3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Seams, gusset, hem, and the quiet geometry that keeps a garment legible after washing. The sample is small by design; the conclusions are provisional."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "81bed5593d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Research at the Institute begins with a person who has been sitting for four hours. Not a model, not a mirror, not a fitting room with the door closed. The garment is studied where it is asked to hold: under tailoring, on a night train, in a warm room, after the meeting has run late."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "b5831d86d5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A finding is a sentence the evidence can carry. Where the evidence is thin, the sentence is shorter. Where the finding changes, the correction stays in the record beside the claim it replaced. This is slower than opinion and less satisfying than a slogan, which is why the Institute keeps doing it."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "109e41f8c2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The programme is not market research. A preference may be recorded, but it is not promoted to evidence. The panel observes conditions, repeats them where it can, and states the limits before it states the conclusion. The Index is an annual edition with periodic revisions; the research record is continuous."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "026c29515f", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Current studies", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "9cd4d45376", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The current programme is deliberately small. Each study addresses one question and runs until the panel can describe the result without adjectives. Studies are listed with their status and their limits; a study without a stated limit is not ready to be listed."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "c097046c7b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Study 01 — The Seated Hour. A continuing observation of waistband behaviour across a working day. Assessed seated, standing, and in transition. The panel records adjustments, not impressions. Status: in progress; observations recorded through Q4 2026."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "ed34669c13", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Study 02 — Laundry and Legibility. What survives the wash: seam geometry, hem behaviour, and the quiet arithmetic of shrinkage. Conducted with the Institute's standard wash protocol and recorded against the care reference published with each garment. Status: in progress; first review January 2027."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "188c75e6b7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Study 03 — The Hotel Drawer. An occasional study of garments encountered away from home. The sample is opportunistic and the conclusions are correspondingly modest. Status: occasional; next review January 2027."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "b87813b8b4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Method", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "92742abb04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each study names its question before it begins. Conditions are repeated, observations are logged, and the panel's median is preferred to its mean, because the mean rewards enthusiasm. A result is published with its method attached; a result without a method is an anecdote."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "38c26d2c24", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sessions are conducted seated where possible. The panel is asked to describe the day, not the garment. Adjustments are counted without interpretation. Where a garment performs well, the panel is asked what else was true: the room, the chair, the hour, the outer layer. Comfort is a claim; composure is evidence."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "b88541e451", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Institute does not confuse a laboratory with a life. A garment that works only in a fitting room has been flattered, not tested. The method is designed to make flattery difficult and to leave the finding open to revision."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "d456ef9d58", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The standing panel", "level": 2}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "a14271c318", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The panel is small by design. It is composed of people who spend their days in rooms not of their choosing: tailors, archivists, logistics coordinators, and others who work seated for long hours. Members serve for 12 months and are recorded in the panel register."}, "tunes": {"textAlignment": {"alignment": "left"}}}, {"id": "4dd529505c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Assessors are issued garments without labels where the protocol allows. Most can identify the maker anyway. It does not deliberate toward a preference, and it does not produce consensus for publication. It produces observations, which the Institute edits into findings.
